subject: NASA bans AI images instead of checking
thesis: More AI rules arrived this week while nobody is paying anyone to check that they are followed: Taiwan's election deepfake law has not drawn a single takedown request, and NASA stopped trying to tell real images from generated ones and banned AI imagery outright.
ground: The Springer Nature ebooks that UC libraries bought turned out to include machine-summarized titles, and neither the publisher selling them nor the library buying them read them closely enough to stop it. Musixmatch signed Suno as a customer for Sentinel, its copyright-detection tool, and checking only really runs where a company like that is paying for it.

evidence.headline: 대만 선거에 필요한 제대로 된 딥페이크법
evidence.role: It holds up the first half: pass a law, fund nobody to enforce it, and not one takedown request comes in.

evidence.headline: AI 이미지가 넘칠수록 NASA 브랜드는 신뢰를 지킨다
evidence.role: NASA's decision shows what takes the place of checking once an organization cannot afford to vet images one by one.

evidence.headline: 스프링거 네이처의 기계 생성 책, 대학 도서관 서가에 들어왔다
evidence.role: With nobody reading the manuscripts, no one even knows what got through until it is sitting on a university shelf.

evidence.headline: 뮤직스매치 CEO, 가사를 음악 산업의 LLM이라 부르다
evidence.role: Suno becoming a Sentinel customer shows that checking is not free but a product someone has to buy.
